Damage Reduction.description: Upon reaching 20th level, a favored soul obtains damage reduction. A lawful-aligned character receives DR 10/silver, while a chaotic-aligned character receives DR 10/cold iron. If the favored soul is neither lawful nor chaotic, she may select which of the two forms of damage reduction to gain.

Deity's Weapon Focus.description: Starting at 3rd level, a favored soul receives the Weapon Focus feat for her deity's favored weapon at no cost. If she already possesses that feat, she may select a different feat instead.

Deity's Weapon Specialization.description: At 12th level, a favored soul automatically gains the Weapon Specialization feat with her deity's favored weapon. If she already has that feat, she may pick a different feat in its place.

Energy Resistance.description: Beginning at 5th level, a favored soul selects one energy type and gains resistance 10 against it. At 10th level and again at 15th level, she selects an additional energy type and gains resistance 10 against that type as well.

Spells.description: A favored soul draws from the cleric spell list and casts divine spells spontaneously, without needing to prepare them in advance. Casting a spell requires a minimum Charisma score equal to 10 + the spell's level. The saving throw DC for a favored soul's spells equals 10 + spell level + her Wisdom modifier. Her daily spell allotment is limited by class level and she gains bonus spells from a high Charisma score. Unlike a cleric, a favored soul has a restricted number of spells known. She starts play knowing four 0-level and three 1st-level spells, gaining additional spells known as she advances in level. Charisma does not increase the number of spells she knows. Beginning at 4th level and at every even-numbered level thereafter, a favored soul may replace one spell she knows with a different spell of the same level, provided the original spell is at least two levels lower than the highest spell level she can cast. She may exchange only a single spell per level, and must decide whether to swap at the same time she would learn new spells.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency.description: Favored souls have proficiency with all simple weapons, light and medium armor, and shields (but not tower shields). A favored soul also gains proficiency with the favored weapon of her deity. Heavy armor does not interfere with her divine spellcasting, even though she lacks proficiency with it.

Wings.description: At 17th level, a favored soul sprouts wings and gains a fly speed of 60 feet with good maneuverability. A good-aligned favored soul develops feathered wings, while an evil-aligned favored soul grows bat-like wings. A favored soul who is neither good nor evil may choose either wing type.

classFeatures.description: Favored souls are proficient with all simple weapons, with light and medium armor, and with shields (except tower shields). A favored soul is also proficient with her deity's favored weapon. Although a favored soul is not proficient with heavy armor, wearing it does not interfere with her spellcasting.

classFeatures.description: A favored soul casts divine spells (the same type of spells available to clerics), which are drawn from the cleric spell list. She can cast any spell she knows without preparing it ahead of time the way a cleric must. To cast a spell, a favored soul must have a Charisma score of 10 + the spell's level (Cha 10 for 0-level spells, Cha 11 for 1st-level spells, and so forth). The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a favored soul's spell is 10 + the spell's level + the favored soul's Wisdom modifier. Like other spellcasters, a favored soul can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. Her base daily spell allotment is given in the class table. In addition, she receives bonus spells for a high Charisma. Unlike a cleric, a favored soul's selection of spells is limited. A favored soul begins play knowing four 0-level spells and three 1st-level spells of your choice. At each new favored soul level, she gains one or more new spells, as indicated in the class table. (Unlike spells per day, her Charisma score does not affect the number of spells a favored soul knows; the numbers in the class table.) Upon reaching 4th level, and at every even-numbered favored soul level after that (6th, 8th, and so on), a favored soul can choose to learn a new spell in place of one she already knows. In effect, the favored soul "loses" the old spell in exchange for the new one. The new spell's level must be the same as that of the spell being exchanged, and it must be at least two levels lower than the highest-level favored soul spell the favored soul can cast. A favored soul may swap only a single spell at any given level, and must choose whether or not to swap the spell at the same time that she gains new spells known for the level. Unlike a cleric, a favored soul need not prepare her spells in advance. She can cast any spell she knows at any time, assuming she has not yet used up her spells per day for that spell level.
